logline: A Sinaloa woman who witnesses the murder of her drug-runner boyfriend escapes to build a cartel empire of her own - Alice Braga carrying a five-season revenge saga on her shoulders.

renewal.note: Five-season run concluded June 9, 2021 on USA Network. Available on Netflix for streaming.

bollymeter.basis: 68% on Rotten Tomatoes (19 critics), 59 Metascore. Critics called it violent and fun with a strong lead performance but found the pilot season familiar in its genre mechanics.

pull_quotes.text: A violent, fun drama with a great lead performance.

seasons.review_body: Queen of the South premiered on USA Network in June 2016 as an adaptation of Arturo Perez-Reverte's novel and the Spanish telenovela La Reina del Sur. Alice Braga as Teresa Mendoza carried the season on craft alone - critics at a 68% Rotten Tomatoes score (19 reviews) and 59 Metacritic praised her without fully endorsing the show around her. The Season 1 critics' consensus called it a show that 'enlivens an overdone premise with action and narrative vigor.' The show won the 2017 Imagen Award for Best Primetime Drama, a meaningful signal that its Latin representation was landing where it counted. Average viewership of 1.22 million per episode made it a solid cable performer.

episode_reviews.title: Piloto
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Teresa's Sinaloa world with efficiency and then destroys it - putting Braga through an escape sequence that makes the show's stakes immediately physical.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Teresa's flight from Sinaloa - the inciting act that sets the entire five-season trajectory in motion.

bollymeter.basis: 93% on Rotten Tomatoes (3 critics). Small sample but the critical consensus shifted to praise the show's increasingly confident pacing under new showrunner Natalie Chaidez.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired in June 2017 and brought new showrunner Natalie Chaidez, who won a WIN Award in 2018 for a film or show written by a woman. Critics who reviewed it - a small sample of 3 at 93% on RT - noted more agile pacing and Teresa's transition from a reactive survivor to an active architect of her own criminal empire. The season expanded the supporting cast's depth and began building the infrastructure of her eventual operation. Season 2 is where the show found its procedural confidence.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 pivots Teresa from fugitive to operator - the structural shift that makes the later seasons credible.

bollymeter.basis: 80% on Rotten Tomatoes (5 critics). Critics noted the show's willingness to escalate consequences rather than reset, maintaining stakes across three seasons.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 of Queen of the South arrived in June 2018 with Teresa's operation expanding into new territory and new enemies. The RT score of 80% from 5 critics reflected a stable if niche critical profile. The season's most discussed element was its refusal to let Teresa's victories feel permanent - setbacks were written with genuine consequence rather than procedural reset. Viewership remained in cable drama range, averaging well for USA Network's lineup.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 keeps raising the stakes rather than recycling earlier threats - the key discipline that sustains long-form crime dramas.

bollymeter.basis: 83% on Rotten Tomatoes (1 critic). TV Fanatic praised Teresa's continued arc and the show's commitment to its female-driven crime narrative.

pull_quotes.text: It feels good to have the queen back wearing her crown, even if she continues to have to fight for it.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 continued Teresa's consolidation of power in June 2019. With only one aggregated critic review on RT, the season largely played to an established fanbase rather than drawing new critical attention. TV Fanatic's review noted the satisfaction of watching Teresa maintain her position while the show continued to introduce credible antagonists. The season was competent without being revelatory, and viewership held steady.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 4 is consolidation mode - the show in confident autopilot rather than creative reinvention.

bollymeter.basis: 86% on Rotten Tomatoes (3 critics). Critics praised the final season for closing Teresa's arc with intentionality rather than open-ended ambiguity.

seasons.review_body: The final 10-episode season aired from April to June 2021 and earned its best RT score since Season 2 - 86% from 3 critics. The reduced episode count served the story: Season 5 moved with the directness of a show that had its exit in sight and built toward Teresa's final arc without unnecessary detours. Viewership had declined to 0.89 million average per episode from Season 1's 1.22 million, but the 86% RT score from 3 critics reflected a strong close for a show that had spent five seasons earning the ending it delivered.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 5's shortened run is its best decision - a tighter finale arc that closes Teresa's story without overstaying its welcome.
